description: Natural log of night-time radiance per person, ln(10⁸ × NTL / population). description: SDG 1 (No poverty) index of the Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020, on a 0-100 scale where 100 means the goal's targets are met (best value) and 0 the worst situation. Following the global SDG Index method (Lafortune et al., 2018), each of its 4 indicators is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between a worst value (generally the 2.5th-percentile tail of the municipal distribution) and a best value (the SDG target where one exists, otherwise the average of the five best municipalities, or expert judgement), with the direction set so that higher is always better and values beyond the bounds capped at 0 or 100; the index is the simple (equal-weight) mean of the available rescaled indicators. The components refer to different years; the observatory stores the index at 2016, the latest reference year among them. Where extreme energy poverty is missing (24 municipalities) it is the mean of the other three.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of dwellings that consumed less than a quarter of the Tarifa Dignidad (subsidised tariff) ceiling, i.e. under 210 kWh per year, judged from residential electricity-meter records of May 2016; dwellings without electricity (and so without a meter) also count as extremely energy poor. Built by Andersen, Branisa & Calderón (2019). Reference year 2016. Missing for 24 municipalities. In the SDG 1 index it is normalised linearly between 94.9 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; SDG target / leave no one behind), values beyond the bounds capped.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Percentage of the population with Unsatisfied Basic Needs (NBI) in 2012, INE's official municipal poverty measure (housing, basic services, energy, education and health deprivations), computed from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE). source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Alkire-Foster multidimensional poverty index (0-1) for 2012 with 9 household deprivations: an illiterate member, a member over 6 without an identity document, no fixed or mobile phone, a birth outside a health facility in the last 5 years, a teenage pregnancy in the last 5 years, a child aged 6-19 not studying, no drinking water on the property, no electricity, no basic sanitation. In the SDG 1 index it is normalised linearly between 0.391 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; leave no one behind), values beyond the bounds capped.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Gender parity index of secondary-school dropout, 2017, from Ministry of Education records (SEIE). The goal is one-directional: women should be at least as well off as men. In the SDG 5 index it is normalised linearly between 0 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 1 (best; SDG target: parity; values above 1 count as 100), values beyond the bounds capped.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Annual deforestation rate, average of 2016-2018, as a percentage of the forest area in 2015, computed by Conservación Internacional Bolivia from satellite data (Hansen et al. 2013, Global Forest Change v1.5). Stored at 2017, the period midpoint. In the SDG 13 index it is normalised linearly between 5.44 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 0 (best; average of the top 5), values beyond the bounds capped.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Estimated municipal population in 2020 (persons), as printed in the Atlas municipal profiles ("Población estimada, 2020"). The Atlas does not name the source; the 339 values sum to 11,633,371, exactly INE's 2020 national population projection (Revisión 2020 series), so they are presumably INE's municipal projections. Not an input of any goal index. Differs from the gridded WorldPop-based pop dataset.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Share of the municipal population living in urban areas in 2012 (%), as printed in the Atlas municipal profiles ("Tasa de urbanización, 2012"), from the 2012 Population and Housing Census (INE). INE counts as urban the localities with 2,000 or more inhabitants, which is why 175 municipalities have a rate of 0. Not an input of any goal index (the Atlas treats 15 almost fully urban municipalities as having no applicable farm indicators for SDG 2; 11 of them are 95% or more urban by this rate, while Sucre, Tiquipaya and Potosí are 91–92% and Yunguyo de Litoral 0%).
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: GDO-Bolivia municipality geo ID (BO-DD-PP-MM) of the 339-unit municipality map, numbered as in GADM 4.1; its boundary in geo/boundaries/ comes from geoBoundaries (GeoBolivia, public domain). It nests by prefix into the department (BO-DD) and province (BO-DD-PP) IDs; department and province numbers follow GADM order and differ from INE codes.

Reference year of the values in the row. Each SDG Atlas variable is stored only at its own reference year (geo:year); indicators averaged over a period are stored at the period's midpoint, rounded down, and the goal index at the latest reference year of its indicators, so the panel is sparse.

Official municipality code of the National Statistics Institute (INE), DDPPMM (department, province, municipality) stored as an integer without the leading zero (e.g. 20101 = La Paz). The Atlas indicators are linked to geo_id through this code, which places DS4Bolivia's three swapped homonym pairs in their correct municipality.
source: INE via DS4Bolivia

description: SDG 15 (Life on land) index of the Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020, on a 0-100 scale where 100 means the goal's targets are met (best value) and 0 the worst situation. Following the global SDG Index method (Lafortune et al., 2018), each of its 2 indicators is rescaled linearly to 0-100 between a worst value (generally the 2.5th-percentile tail of the municipal distribution) and a best value (the SDG target where one exists, otherwise the average of the five best municipalities, or expert judgement), with the direction set so that higher is always better and values beyond the bounds capped at 0 or 100; the index is the simple (equal-weight) mean of the available rescaled indicators. Components: Protected areas (% of area); Biodiversity loss from deforestation. The components refer to different years; the observatory stores the index at 2019, the latest reference year among them.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Legally declared protected area (national, departmental and municipal) as a percentage of the municipality's area, 2019, computed by Conservación Internacional Bolivia for the Atlas. 200 municipalities have 0; two slightly exceed 100 in the source data. In the SDG 15 index it is normalised linearly between 0 (worst; 2.5th-percentile tail) and 50 (best; global SDG Index; 50% or more scores 100), values beyond the bounds capped.
source: Municipal Atlas of the SDGs in Bolivia 2020

description: Biodiversity loss index due to deforestation, average of 2016-2018: a species disturbance index (Andersen & Ledezma, 2019, with Conservación Internacional Bolivia) that weights deforested habitat by the number of species present there, all species weighted equally.
